subject: Stellaris Order Form - SLA alternatives & maintenance proposal
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@stellarishealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: David Park <david.park@stellarishealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MSA + SLA redlines attached

Mateo,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the order form. We reviewed the draft MSA and the SLA exhibit and attached a redline (Stellaris_MSA_redline_v1.pdf) with comments focused on availability guarantees and maintenance carveouts. High level asks from the Stellaris side:

- Uptime: we need 99.99% monthly availability for production inference endpoints.
- Service credits: request a stepped credit scale starting at 5% for <99.99%, increasing to 20% for outages under 95%.
- Response times: P1 incident response within 15 minutes and roll-up to engineering within 1 hour.
- Maintenance: no maintenance windows that would impact 02:00-08:00 ET for our east-coast systems; prefer Saturday or Sunday 03:00-06:00 PT if unavoidable.

We want to get legal and ops aligned this week. Can you confirm Redwood's position on these four items and propose tradeoffs? If we can agree on the SLA terms we can move the order form to signature.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Procurement
Stellaris Health

Thanks Elena — got the redline and noted the four asks. Looping Hannah (legal) and Lauren (ops) to put together our proposed compromises.

Quick response while they dig in:
- Uptime: 99.99% is a high bar for inference at scale; we can present alternative formulations (see options to follow).
- Credits: we have a standard stepped credit schedule but are open to enlarging the top-end for critical infra with a capped annual credit.
- P1 response: we treat P1s as urgent; our typical SLA is initial response within 30 minutes and engagement at engineering within 1 hour — we'll see if we can compress the initial ack window.
- Maintenance: we can avoid east-coast 02:00-08:00 ET if we can schedule weekly windows outside your peak periods; ops to propose windows.

I'll circulate proposed options and a short one-pager to make tradeoffs clear. Want to set a 30-minute call tomorrow to align?

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood legal summary - Stellaris SLA positions (internal)

Team,

I reviewed Stellaris' redline and compiled the positions we should take and where we can be flexible. I attached a short diff (redwood-sla-options-diff.docx). Key points: 

1) Uptime target
- Stellaris requests 99.99% monthly. Redwood position: standard is 99.95% for inference endpoints.
- Compromise proposal: 99.97% for the production model endpoint(s) that Stellaris designates as "critical" (up to 3 endpoints), with 99.95% baseline for others. This reduces credit exposure while acknowledging their need for higher availability on critical traffic.

2) Service credits
- Stellaris asked for aggressive stepped credits up to 20%. We propose a staircase with caps and an annual maximum credit: 5% credit if monthly availability <99.95% and >=99.90%; 12% if <99.95% and >=99.50%; 20% if <99.50%, capped at 20% of the monthly invoice and an annual cap of 50% of annual spend (protects Redwood from catastrophic exposure).

3) Incident response times
- Stellaris requests P1 initial response 15m and engineering engagement within 1h. Our standard is P1 initial ack within 30m and engineering engagement within 1h.
- Ops note: we can compress initial ack to 20m for customers on a Dedicated or higher-tier SLA (requires product/price change). Option: offer 20m ack + 1h eng for critical endpoints as part of a premium support add-on.

4) Maintenance windows
- Stellaris' east-coast restriction (no maintenance 02:00-08:00 ET) is reasonable. Proposed ops schedule: weekly maintenance baseline Sun 03:00-06:00 PT (which is Sun 06:00-09:00 ET) and an emergency maintenance carveout with 2-hour notice except for critical security patches. We should ask for a 12-hour blackout notice on data migrations.

Negotiation levers: designate critical endpoints, tiered response credits, annual credit cap, and an optional premium support add-on to meet tighter ack windows.

I recommend we present two options to Stellaris:
A) Availability-first: 99.99% for all production endpoints with a higher price and reduced annual credit cap.
B) Targeted-critical approach: 99.97% for up to 3 critical endpoints, 99.95% baseline otherwise + premium support add-on available for 20m ack.

If we go with B we keep managed risk and a clear upsell path.

Hannah
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-sla-options-diff.docx

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Stellaris SLA - two options for tradeoffs (short)

Elena — thanks again for the redline. Attached is a short summary we will use to discuss options on a call (summary in body below).

Option A — Availability-first (fastest path to full uptime)
- 99.99% monthly across all production inference endpoints
- Service credits: stepladder aligned with your request, but monthly credits capped at 20% of the invoice and annual cap at 30% of annual spend (to limit runaway exposure)
- P1 initial ack: 20 minutes (requires premium support add-on), engineering engagement within 1 hour
- Maintenance: we agree to avoid 02:00-08:00 ET windows; weekly maintenance windows scheduled outside your peak if mutually acceptable
- Pricing: premium surcharge to cover reserved capacity and higher SLA guarantees (TBD)

Option B — Targeted-critical (risk-limited, predictable economics)
- 99.97% for up to 3 endpoints you designate as critical; 99.95% baseline for the rest
- Service credits: our proposed staircase (5% / 12% / 20%) with the annual cap at 50% of annual spend
- P1 initial ack: 30 minutes standard; 20 minutes available with premium support add-on; engineering engagement within 1 hour
- Maintenance: weekly baseline Sun 03:00-06:00 PT (avoid your east-coast 02:00-08:00 ET); emergency maint with 2-hour notice for critical fixes
- Pricing: smaller support uplift for targeted-critical coverage

Next steps: pick Option A or B or tell us which levers you want to change. We can schedule a 30-minute call to finalize which endpoints would be designated as critical (if B) and to walk through the pricing delta. My scheduler: https://redwoodinference.app/scheduler/mateo — propose two windows and we will confirm.

Mateo / team — thank you, that is helpful and clear. Stellaris prefers Option B (targeted-critical) with the following asks:

- We will designate two critical endpoints initially (prediction-api and realtime-llm).
- We accept 99.97% for those two and 99.95% baseline for the rest.
- Annual credit cap: we would like the cap to be 40% of annual spend (open to discussion).
- For P1 response: we will purchase the premium support add-on to get the 20-minute ack for critical endpoints (please provide pricing).
- Maintenance: the proposed Sun 03:00-06:00 PT window works; please provide the emergency patch notice and rollback commitments in the exhibit.

We are available for a 30-minute call on Friday Apr 16 at 10:00 AM PT or Monday Apr 19 at 08:00 AM PT — Friday works best for our legal and ops team.

If you can send an updated SLA exhibit reflecting Option B and the two designated endpoints, we can have legal review and be ready to move to signature pending pricing for the premium add-on.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Procurement
Stellaris Health
